body:
Fixes #2839. In the stylist-svelte run (solve 2.34.0, `--tool codex --think xhigh`, Godmy/stylist-svelte#3 → PR #4), `--auto-restart-until-mergeable` spent all 5 restarts (about $2.2 and 33 minutes) on `pipeline-check`. That check fails on `main` and on the solver's own `.gitkeep` commit `73b6c7d` because a private submodule returns 404. Restarts 2/5–5/5 ended on the same SHA `edee6d7` with a clean tree, and each session only reported "CI remains blocked…". The no-progress breaker (#2247/#2313) never fired.

### Change after review ([comment](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2851#issuecomment-6096899740))

An earlier version stopped the loop with a "needs human: CI fails on the base branch too" comment. Per review, that premise was wrong: a pull request with failing CI cannot be released, so every CI failure must be fixed, including pre-existing ones. When CI needs a human action, the pull request's CI should pass and the default branch's CI should say what to do. **The stop is removed.** The restart prompt now asks the AI to fix the CI.

### Root causes

1. **The no-progress fingerprint included the model's final message.** `buildSessionFingerprint` hashed `normalizeSessionMessage(finalMessage)` together with `git status` and `HEAD`. The model reworded its message every time, so `repeated` was never true.
2. **The restart prompt never told the AI how to handle a CI failure it cannot fix directly.** It only said "Please fix the failing CI checks." Each session found that the submodule was private, said so in different words and changed nothing.

### What changes

- **`src/session-progress.lib.mjs`.** The fingerprint is now `git status` and `HEAD` only. The final message is still recorded and quoted in the escalation prompt and the stop comment, but it is not compared. The #2313 rule is unchanged: the first repeat with an unchanged input escalates, and a repeat after the escalation stops. This is the safety net for a real stall.
- **CI restart prompt (`src/solve.auto-merge.lib.mjs` + `buildCiFailureGuidance`).** Every CI restart now says:
  - fix every failing check, including failures that also happen on the default branch, because the pull request cannot be merged or released while its CI fails;
  - if a check can only pass after a human action (a secret, access to a private repository or submodule), change CI/CD so that **CI on the pull request passes without that action** (skip only that step and print why), and **CI on the default branch fails with an explicit message saying exactly what a human has to do**, so the job can be re-run once that is done;
  - describe the manual action in the PR description.
- **`buildAutoRestartInstructions`.** "Ensure you comply with all CI/CD check requirements, and they pass" now adds "including checks that already fail on the default branch".
- **`src/ci-pre-existing-failure.lib.mjs` (new): evidence only, no stop.** A failing check is *pre-existing* when the check with the same name also failed on the current head of the base branch (checked first) or on the placeholder commit. When every failing check is pre-existing, the prompt lists the failing commits as links and says "That does not make them optional: they still block this pull request, so fix them here". This saves the AI a session spent finding out that the failure is not its own. Lookup errors return `null`, and then no evidence is added. It uses `gh api` check-runs plus commit statuses.
- **Guarding the fingerprint change.** The message no longer tells sessions apart, so a restart triggered by a new human comment or issue edit skips the no-progress check. A human's request is new work even if the previous session changed nothing.

On the stylist-svelte run, the next session would be told to make `pipeline-check` pass on the PR, for example by skipping the private-submodule step when it has no access, with an explicit failure message on `main`. If it still changed nothing, the no-progress breaker would escalate once and then stop, instead of spending 5/5.

### Codebase audit against the principle ([comment](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2851#issuecomment-6106280067))

I searched `src/` for anything that exempts, skips or stops on a pre-existing CI failure (`pre-existing`, `already fail`, `unrelated`, `base branch`, `flaky`, every CI feedback and stop site):

- **System prompts did not say it.** The finalize checklist only said "check that all CI checks are passing if they exist before you finish", and Gemini's prompt did not ask about CI at all. All six tool prompts (`claude`, `codex`, `agent`, `opencode`, `qwen`, `gemini`) and the four `src/locales/*.lino` catalogues now add "including checks that already fail on the default branch (when a check needs a human action, make CI on the pull request pass without it and CI on the default branch fail with an explicit message saying what to do)".
- **Watch mode (`src/solve.watch.lib.mjs`).** Its no-progress check now also skips when a new human comment arrived, the same as `--auto-restart-until-mergeable`. Without this, the fingerprint change could stop the loop right after a human asked for something.
- **Checked and left as they are:** in-session CI frames (`bidirectional-interactive.lib.mjs`) and the feedback "Failed pull request checks" (`solve.feedback.lib.mjs`) already ask to address every failing check. The stops for an Actions billing limit, a cancelled run that cannot be re-run, and an exhausted external-review quota are not failing checks the AI can fix in code. Stale-rollup reconciliation only drops failures when GitHub itself reports `CLEAN`.
- **Noted, not changed:** the Telegram `/merge` queue (#1341/#2404) refuses to start while the default branch is red. With the approach above, a default branch that is red on purpose (waiting for a human action) blocks the queue until that action is done. That is intended (#2404), so it is not changed here.

### Dependency refresh (freshness gate)

`Checks and release` [38090326023](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/38090326023) failed in `detect-changes` because 7 pins went stale on `main` while the PR was open. Following the approach above, the PR fixes that failure even though it also exists on `main`: Bun 1.4.2 → 1.4.3 (installed over Box's Bun), start-command 0.36.0 → 0.37.0, prettier ^3.9.9 → ^3.9.10. The pin tests (#2187, #2189) were updated to match. After the merge with `main`, [38123052448](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/38123052448) flagged two more use-m pins in `src/use-with-retry.lib.mjs`: command-stream 2.0.0 → 2.0.2 and links-notation 0.25.1 → 0.25.2 (`tests/test-use-with-retry.mjs` and `tests/test-preinstall-use-m-packages-1724.mjs` updated; `experiments/issue-2839/use-m-pins-2.0.2-smoke.mjs` loads both through use-m and runs commands and a parse). `scripts/check-dependency-freshness.mjs` now reports 168/168 current.

### Reproduction and tests

| Test | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/no-progress-paraphrased-messages-2839.test.mjs` (new, default suite) | the four real paraphrased messages on `edee6d7` with a clean tree give one fingerprint and `repeated = true` (the old code gives `false`); escalate-then-stop sequence; `summarizeCommitChecks`, `classifyPreExistingCiFailures`, `detectPreExistingCiFailures` against a fake `gh api` reproducing `pipeline-check` failing on `main` and `73b6c7d`; the guidance requires fixing pre-existing failures (PR passes, default branch explains the manual step); the evidence says "does not make them optional" and never offers stopping; no `ci_fails_on_base_branch` stop reason exists; wiring and the human-feedback exemption |
| `tests/no-progress-between-sessions-2247.test.mjs` (updated) | rewording the message now gives an *equal* fingerprint; git status and HEAD still cannot bleed into each other |
| same file, prompt and watch checks | every tool's system prompt (and `en.lino`) requires fixing pre-existing failures; watch mode skips the no-progress check on a new human comment |
| `experiments/issue-2839-command-stream-path-interpolation.mjs` | command-stream leaves branch names with `/` unquoted inside `repos/…/git/ref/heads/${baseBranch}` |

To reproduce the original bug on `main`: record two outcomes with the same `head` and an empty `gitStatus` but differently worded `finalMessage`s. `recordSessionOutcome(...).repeated` is `false`.

Locally:
- `npm run lint`, `prettier --check` and `scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh` pass.
- The #2247, #2313, #2397, #2182, #2119, #1323, #1567, #1664, #1356, #1570, #1821 and #661 auto-restart and billing tests pass.
- `tests/test-billing-limit-detection.mjs` fails 1/57 with and without this change (it calls the live `gh` API).

### Assumptions

- The default branch's CI "explicitly tells what to do" by failing with a clear message, so it can be re-run once the human action is done. The pull request's CI skips only the step that needs the missing access.
title: fix(auto-merge): no-progress ignores reworded messages; ask AI to fix pre-existing CI failures
